explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/929: "It is trivial that S(k) ≤ k+1 since, for example, one can take n ≡ 1 (mod (k+1)!)." The Lean S k is sInf of x : ℕ such that {n | each of n+1,…,n+k has a prime factor ≤ x} has positive density, and the theorem asserts S k ≤ k + 1 for all k. Verified: for n ≡ 1 mod (k+1)!, n+i ≡ 1+i (mod (k+1)!) and (1+i) | (k+1)!, so 1+i ∈ [2,k+1] divides n+i, giving a prime factor ≤ k+1; this residue class has density 1/(k+1)! > 0. Holds also for k = 0, 1. Faithful and true.
